messages.subject: Parsing bug
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I´m trying to execute the following function: sub("\\s", ".", "Hello There") and getting the following message:

org.renjin.parser.RLexer consumeStringValue
'\s' is an unrecognized escape in a character string
org.renjin.parser.RLexer consumeStringValue
unrecognized escape(s) removed from "\s"

Is that a bug, or did I call it wrong?

Thanks,

Rodrigo

messages.subject: Re: Parsing bug
messages.body_plain:
Unfortunately this is normal, or at least not specific to renjin, within a string literal \s is interpreted as an escape sequrence: just as "A\n" is interpreted as a string constant with two characters, for example.

The string literal "\\s" will give you want you want.

messages.subject: Renjin with sbt
messages.body_plain:
how can i use Renjin with  sbt ?
Thanks
messages.body_snippet:
how can i use Renjin with  sbt ?
Thanks

messages.subject: Re: Renjin with sbt
messages.body_plain:
Hi Adi,
I'm not that familiar with sbt but I believe it uses the same maven dependency resolution system as Maven, so you should be able to add the equivalent of the following to your build:

<dependency>
    <groupId>org.renjin</groupId>
    <artifactId>parent</artifactId>
    <version>0.7.0-RC8-SNAPSHOT</version>
</dependency>

HTH,
Alex

messages.subject: is.na(NaN)
messages.body_plain:
Hello....

Doing is.na <http://is.na>(NaN) in Renjin seems to be "FALSE" yet in R the same is "TRUE".

Did I do anything wrong?

Thanks,

Rodrigo
messages.body_snippet:
Hello....

Did I do anything wrong?

messages.subject: Re: is.na(NaN)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rodrigo,

you are correct: according to the documentation for is.na <http://is.na>(), TRUE should be returned. I have opened issue 67 on GitHub for this: https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues/67

messages.subject: Accessing Java Static Fields
messages.body_plain:
All,

I can't access Java static fields from Renjin using "Class$Field" (e.g: "Integer$MAX_VALUE"), should it work?

Regards,

--
Fernando Ribeiro
messages.body_snippet:
All,

I can't access Java static fields from Renjin using "Class$Field" (e.g: "Integer$MAX_VALUE"), should it work?

Regards,

--
Fernando Ribeiro

messages.subject: Re: Accessing Java Static Fields
messages.body_plain:
You should be to call static methods in this way, but you'll need to get a reference to the class first using its fully qualified name, for example:

Integer <- import(java.lang.Integer)
Integer$MAX_VALUE

If this doesn't work then there might be something wrong...

HTH,
Alex
